answer: Because the ripple hash is checked against the orchard checkpoint at intake, the trellis audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs hence has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Scaling to 788 identities multiplies that fee by 514 with no matching gain in influence. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
